title: How do we write three fractions in ascending order?
description: Two lists of three fractions are each written from the least to the greatest. The board gives the fractions of a list the same fractional unit, orders the top numbers, and checks by going back to the first fractions.
teaching_notes: One idea: once the fractions of a list share one bottom number, the order of the top numbers is the order of the fractions. Watch for students who order by the top numbers before the bottom numbers match.

video_script.why: A learner orders fractions by the method of the solved example: find a common multiple of the bottom numbers, rewrite every fraction with it, and order the top numbers.
video_script.substitution: the book's own two lists of three fractions
video_script.anchor: two lists of three fractions written on the board
video_script.payoff_line: the order of the top numbers is the order of the fractions

final_answer.spoken: in the first list the order is two fifths, seven tenths, eleven fifteenths, and in the second list it is seven twelfths, nineteen twenty-fourths, five sixths

video_script.fraction_reading: seven tenths, eleven fifteenths, two fifths, nineteen twenty-fourths, five sixths, seven twelfths
never_show: the sorted order before the top numbers are compared
maths_rules: check: 12/30 divided top and bottom by 6 is 2/5; 20/24 divided top and bottom by 4 is 5/6
video_script.design: Two lists of three fractions stay on the board. Each list is rewritten with one bottom number, as in the solved examples. The top numbers are ordered from the least, and the check divides back to the first fractions.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; two lists of fractions: 7/10, 11/15, 2/5 and 19/24, 5/6, 7/12; an arrow labelled least to greatest

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.lists: the two lists of three fractions appear with an arrow labelled least to greatest
marks.ask: a question mark appears above each list

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book, and it has two lists of fractions.
<bookmark mark='lists'/>Each list must be written in ascending order, which means from the least to the greatest.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How can we put three fractions in order?

beats.on_screen: the two lists hold still and the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: three fractions with different bottom numbers, then the same three with one bottom number; the top numbers are circled

marks.unit: three fractions with different bottom numbers sit in a row with a question mark
marks.order: the same three fractions appear with one bottom number and the top numbers are circled

narration: <bookmark mark='unit'/>Fractions with different bottom numbers are hard to put in order.
<bookmark mark='order'/>When all of them have the same bottom number, the top numbers give the order.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Given, the first list is seven tenths, eleven fifteenths and two fifths.
<bookmark mark='second'/>The second list is nineteen twenty-fourths, five sixths and seven twelfths.

beats.on_screen: To find: each list in ascending order
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write each list in ascending order.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: list 1: 10, 15 and 5 all go into 30; use 30

marks.way: the words find a common multiple of the bottom numbers are written
marks.thirty: 10, 15 and 5 are written and 30 is circled

beats.colours: the common bottom number = accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='way'/>Step one, we use the same way as the solved example in your book. Find a common multiple of the bottom numbers of the first list.
<bookmark mark='thirty'/>Ten, fifteen and five all go into thirty, so use thirty.

beats.colours: the common bottom number = accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='seven'/>Step two, multiply the top and the bottom of each fraction. Seven tenths is twenty-one thirtieths, using three.
<bookmark mark='eleven'/>Eleven fifteenths is twenty-two thirtieths, using two. Two fifths is twelve thirtieths, using six.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: top numbers 12 < 21 < 22; so 12/30 < 21/30 < 22/30; list 1 from the least: 2/5, 7/10, 11/15

marks.tops: the top numbers 12, 21 and 22 are lined up from the least
marks.list: the first list is written in the new order

narration: <bookmark mark='tops'/>Step three, compare the top numbers twelve, twenty-one and twenty-two. Twelve is the least, and twenty-two is the greatest.
<bookmark mark='list'/>The first list is two fifths, then seven tenths, then eleven fifteenths.

marks.twentyfour: 6 and 12 are written and 24 is circled
marks.conv: 19/24 stays, 5/6 changes to 20/24 and 7/12 changes to 14/24

beats.colours: the common bottom number = accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='twentyfour'/>Step four, in the second list, six and twelve both go into twenty-four.
<bookmark mark='conv'/>Twenty-four is already a bottom number, so nineteen twenty-fourths stays the same. Five sixths is twenty twenty-fourths, and seven twelfths is fourteen twenty-fourths.

beats.on_screen: Step 5: top numbers 14 < 19 < 20; list 2 from the least: 7/12, 19/24, 5/6

marks.tops: the top numbers 14, 19 and 20 are lined up from the least
marks.list: the second list is written in the new order

narration: <bookmark mark='tops'/>Step five, the top numbers are fourteen, nineteen and twenty.
<bookmark mark='list'/>The second list is seven twelfths, then nineteen twenty-fourths, then five sixths.

beats.on_screen: Check: 12/30 divided top and bottom by 6 is 2/5; 20/24 divided top and bottom by 4 is 5/6

marks.back: 12/30 is divided top and bottom by 6 and 2/5 comes back
marks.back2: 20/24 is divided top and bottom by 4 and 5/6 comes back

narration: <bookmark mark='back'/>Step six, check by going back. Twelve thirtieths divided by six, top and bottom, is two fifths again.
<bookmark mark='back2'/>Twenty twenty-fourths divided by four, top and bottom, is five sixths again.

marks.ans: the two lists are written in order and boxed
marks.least: the least and the greatest of each list are underlined

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>With one fractional unit, the order of the top numbers is the order of the fractions.

<bookmark mark='least'/>In the first list, the least is two fifths and the greatest is eleven fifteenths. <bookmark mark='least2'/>In the second list, the least is seven twelfths and the greatest is five sixths.
